This section examines Experiment P —
sin-dee scientific pipeline ordering

from first principles. Keep two questions
separate: does changing the

order change the measured outcome, and
does the proposed search

method beat a matched alternative at the
same distinct-evaluation budget?

Pipeline components: CLIP, SUBSAMPLE,
SMOOTH, TRIM, MEDIAN, and

DIFFERENTIATE. All 720 orderings
enumerated deterministically. Objective:

recover governing equations; fitness
derived from relative coefficient

error. Result: recovery error ranged from
0.1% to 23.2% by
ordering alone. Best reported ordering:

CLIP→SUBSAMPLE→SMOOTH→TRIM→MEDIAN→DIFFERENTIATE.
Pre-flight: F D C +0.109,

treated as borderline under Decision D19.
Search race: random succeeded

40/40, prism 38/40. Interpretation: order
mattered greatly, but evolutionary

locality was not the best exploitation
mechanism. Now read evidence

panel P-sciml. The axes, units, and sample
are stated on

screen. The sample represented here is All
720 orderings. Raw

observations remain visible wherever the
artifact provides them. Censored

observations stay marked at the cap rather
than becoming invented

hitting times, and sampled landscapes
leave unobserved permutations blank.

The supported finding is: Result: recovery
error ranged from 0.1%

to 23.2% by ordering alone. The broader
claim not established

here is: The conclusion is scoped to the
recorded evaluator,

landscape, and budget. This evidence
changed the program as follows:

Pre-flight: F D C +0.109, treated as
borderline under Decision

D19. The distinction is part of the
result. A large

ordering effect does not automatically
imply an evolutionary-search

advantage, and almost-sure convergence
does not promise practical
efficiency.
